question.text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the midpoint of the guidance range for Q4 FY2027 as stated in NVIDIA’s “Outlook” section of its Q3 FY2027 earnings press release, expected to be published on [NVIDIA’s investor relations site](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/) and the [SEC’s EDGAR system](https://www.sec.gov/) on November 17, 2026.

The unit value for revenues is billions of U.S. dollars, and it will be rounded to the nearest billion. GAAP gross margin will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent. GAAP operating expenses are in a unit value of billions of U.S. dollars and will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a billion dollars.
question.fine_print:
* If a single figure (not a range) is provided, that figure will be used.
* If multiple ranges or scenarios are presented, the primary range specified in the official “Outlook” or “Guidance” section will be used to resolve the subquestions.
* If NVIDIA does not issue guidance for Q4 FY2027 in the Q3 FY2027 release, the corresponding subquestion will be **annulled**.
* Only the originally published figure will be used; subsequent updates, corrections, or guidance revisions will be ignored.

research:
Management already gave a soft guide in August: Q4 FY27 gross margin would bottom in the 71-72% range. Since GAAP and non-GAAP guidance are now nearly identical, the GAAP midpoint looks most likely to land around 71.0-72.0%. That fits inside the question's 68.95-73.05 range. The actual Q4 figure is not out yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-26: The Q2 FY27 release guided Q3 FY27 gross margin to "GAAP and non-GAAP... 74.0%, plus or minus 50 basis points." Q2 actual margin was 75.0% on both GAAP and non-GAAP (Q1 FY27: 74.9% GAAP). [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027)
- The Q3 FY27 release, which will contain the Q4 outlook, is due 2026-11-17 after the market closes. It has not been published yet. [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/nvidia-stock-nvda-stays-under-pressure-amid-ceo-probe-wells-fargo-lowers-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet, but there is a strong anchor:
- 2026-08-26: On the Q2 call, CFO Colette Kress said margins would fall to about 74% in Q3 and then "[hit] bottom" in the 71-72% range in Q4. She blamed "extreme pricing conditions in memory," saying memory prices "exceeded our prior expectations and [are] headed even higher into next year." [TechTarget](https://www.techtarget.com/news/Nvidia-price-hike-will-raise-IT-costs-for-all-analysts-say/856987/), [Webull/Benzinga](https://www.webull.com/news/15475038024909824)
- One secondary summary (Zacks, which I could not fetch) reportedly calls the 71-72% figure non-GAAP. Since Q1 FY27, non-GAAP no longer excludes stock-based compensation, so GAAP and non-GAAP margin guidance now differ by 0 to 0.1 points (Q2 guide: 74.9% GAAP vs 75.0% non-GAAP; Q3 guide: 74.0% vs 74.0%). [NVIDIA Q1 FY27](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027)
- Management expects a recovery to 72-73% in FY28 once price increases take effect. [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/nvidia-stock-nvda-stays-under-pressure-amid-ceo-probe-wells-fargo-lowers-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Previews say Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12 and Kress is now interim CEO; this will be her first report in that role. Visible Alpha consensus for Q3 revenue is about $109.3B. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/tr/haber/2026/11/13/nvidia-kazanc-onizlemesi-kressin-huang-olmadan-ilk-sinavinda-neler-beklenmeli/), [Borsainside](https://www.borsainside.com/news/nvidia-trimestrale-novembre-2026-ricavi-datacenter-huang-previsioni/), [Zacks](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3029813/boardroom-drama-ahead-of-nvidia-s-q3-earnings-buy-or-sell-the-stock)
- 2026-11-13: Cisco reported record AI-driven results and raised guidance, a sign that demand is still strong. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/13/cisco-csco-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/)
- 2026-11-11/12: The WSJ reported the board was considering removing Huang, and the stock fell more than 8% after hours. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/gr/news/2026/11/12/is-nvidia-still-a-good-buy-after-the-stock-sell-off/)
- 2026-11-10: Wells Fargo's Aaron Rakers expects Q4 guidance above consensus ($126.4B revenue vs Street $124.3B) and says he will watch gross margin commentary closely. [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/nvidia-stock-nvda-stays-under-pressure-amid-ceo-probe-wells-fargo-lowers-price-target-ahead-of-q3-earnings)
- 2026 (date not confirmed): Long-term supply commitments rose to $279B from $119B, mostly for memory. [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4960708-nvidia-q3-fy2027-preview-the-fabless-model-just-got-a-279-billion-footnote), [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/nvidia-q3-fy2027-preview-279-billion-supply/)
- One preview expects Q3 actual gross margin around 74.5%, but it is not authoritative. [GamesReviews headline](https://gamesreviews.com/news/08/nvidia-guides-gross-margin-down-to-74-in-q3-71-72-low-in-q4-fy27/) (returned a 403 error, so I only saw the headline)

## 4. Base rates
Recent GAAP gross margin guidance midpoints, compared with the actual results:
- Q2 FY26 guide: 71.8% (non-GAAP 72.0%) (from memory, not re-verified)
- Q3 FY26 guide: 73.3% (non-GAAP 73.5%) (from memory)
- Q4 FY26 guide: 74.8% (non-GAAP 75.0%) (from memory)
- 2026-05-20: Q2 FY27 guide was 74.9% GAAP; the actual came in at 75.0%. [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027)
- 2026-08-26: Q3 FY27 guide was 74.0% GAAP, a 0.9-point step down. [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027)

What the pattern shows:
- Quarter-to-quarter changes in the guided midpoint have usually been between 0.1 and 1.5 points.
- NVIDIA tends to guide close to the actual result, usually within about ±0.3 points.
- When NVIDIA has previously signalled a margin path ahead of time (for example, "mid-70s by year end" in FY26), the later formal guidance has generally matched it.
- The question is a quarterly reporting event, so seasonal patterns don't apply.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket on Q3 actual non-GAAP gross margin: 73-75% at 85.5%; 75-77% at 6.5%; 71-73% at 5.2%. This is about Q3 actuals, not the Q4 guide.
- Polymarket gives a 90.6% chance NVIDIA beats earnings.
- Kalshi gives a 4% chance the earnings call is postponed.
- I could not find any market or published consensus specifically on the Q4 gross margin guidance midpoint. Analyst notes simply repeat the 71-72% "bottom."

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-17, after the close: the Q3 FY27 release, with the Q4 outlook and CFO commentary.
- Factors that could move the number:
  - Memory pricing could rise further, which would push the guide toward or below 71%.
  - Price increases to customers could be passed through faster, which would push the guide toward or above 72%.
  - The change in leadership might make the guidance more conservative. This is speculation; I found no reporting on it.
- A 4% risk of postponement remains; a delay could push the release past the question's expected timing.

- 2026-08-26: CNBC reported that NVIDIA "expects gross margin to decline and bottom out in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, in the range of 71% to 72%, partially due to memory prices." [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/26/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q2-2027-live-updates.html)
- Other reports of the same call: CFO Colette Kress said margins hit "bottom" at 71% to 72% in Q4, then recover to 72% to 73% in FY2028 "as executed price increases take effect in [fiscal] Q1." She cited "extreme pricing conditions in memory," with prices that have "exceeded our prior expectations" and are "headed even higher into next year." [Webull](https://www.webull.com/news/15475038024909824), [KuCoin, 2026-09-22](https://www.kucoin.com/blog/nvidia-memory-prices-hbm-shortage-2030)

## 4. Base rates
- NVIDIA always gives its gross margin guide as a midpoint plus or minus 50 basis points. Recent GAAP midpoints and actuals:
  - Q1 FY2027 actual: 74.9%
  - Q2 FY2027 actual: 75.0%
  - Q3 FY2027 guide: 74.0%
  - Q2 FY2026 actual: 72.4%
- From memory, not verified this session: in FY2026, Kress signaled margins in the "mid-70s" by year end, and the Q4 FY2026 GAAP guide came in at about 74.8%. That would be an example of an earlier qualitative signal being met.
- If the guide follows the signaled band, the likely midpoints are 71.0%, 71.5% or 72.0%. If memory costs got worse since August, as Kress warned they might, it could come in lower, around 70.5% to 71%.
- Seasonality does not apply here; it is a quarterly reporting cycle.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, on Q3 actual non-GAAP gross margin, which is a related question but not this one: 73% to 75% at 85.5%; 71% to 73% at 5.2%; under 71% at 2.9%. That is consistent with Q3 landing near the 74% guide.
- Kalshi gives a 4% chance the earnings call is postponed.
- Polymarket gives a 90.6% chance NVIDIA beats earnings estimates.
- I found no prediction market or published analyst consensus on the Q4 GAAP gross margin guide itself.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-17 after the close: Q3 FY2027 release and earnings call. This is the resolution event.
- Risks to the timing or content of the guide: the leadership transition (Kalshi puts postponement at 4%), any further change in memory and HBM prices, the Rubin ramp mix, and inventory or purchase-commitment charges. Charges like these would hit GAAP and non-GAAP equally under the current reporting policy.
